root_cause: The payments-api HTTP client has no connection reuse, so every partner call opens a new outbound connection; with 24 nodes sharing a single outbound IP and allocatedOutboundPorts at the default, the outbound load balancer's SNAT pool reaches port exhaustion during peak connection churn.
evidence: kql-snat-connection-count.csv: SNATConnectionCount State=Failed spikes from single digits to 700+ only within the 14:00-15:00 UTC peak window
az-aks-show.json: loadBalancerProfile has one managed outbound IP and allocatedOutboundPorts 0 (the default 1024 SNAT ports per node), while nodepool1 runs 24 nodes
kubectl-get-nodes.txt: all 24 nodes of nodepool1 are Ready — the node fleet shares that single outbound IP
app-config.yaml: the partner-settlement client sets keep-alive: false, so every partner call opens a fresh outbound connection
partner-status.json: the partner reports all systems operational with no active incidents — the outage theory is ruled out
payments-api.log: connect timeouts (not latency) at ~5% of partner calls during the same peak window
fix: Configure an Azure NAT gateway as the cluster's outbound path (or increase allocated outbound ports and add outbound IP addresses), and enable HTTP keep-alive with connection pooling in the payments-api client so outbound connections are reused.
